title: Financial help for parents in the ECDA Childminding Pilot for Infants
asked: The MP asked whether parents of infants in the Early Childhood Development Agency's Childminding Pilot can get financial assistance beyond Child Development Account funds, and what other schemes exist to help them cover the cost of these services.
response: The Government subsidises childminding services under the pilot so they are affordable: parents using them full-time, five days a week for four weeks, pay around $700 a month out-of-pocket, against a usual market cost of around $1,200 to $2,800 a month. More than 80% of enrolled families have used their infant's CDA monies to defray out-of-pocket expenses. In reply to a supplementary question, Mr Goh said the pilot runs at two centres with no more than 100 infants, and currently offers only supply-side subsidies to operators plus CDA monies; lower-income families needing infant care are recommended to Government-supported preschools, where means-tested subsidies and fee caps mean they can pay as low as $40 a month for full-day infant care at Anchor Operator preschools.
